correctness.rationale: Every overlap-free word through length 48 is generated by the exact suffix-period predicate. An integer dynamic recurrence over all possible nonempty square suffixes counts ordered nine-square factorizations. It evaluates all 7,867 admissible binary words, finding exactly two length-48 words with one factorization each and none shorter. An independent 74-block enumeration has a proved square-root cutoff 16 and an independent global overlap predicate, reproducing the same two unique witnesses. Both executable sources and exact recorded outputs are embedded. The finite exhaustion implies a global minimum because one witness of length 48 exists; it does not imply classification of longer witnesses.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The maximal *number* of square factors is a different optimization from minimal *total word length* at factor count nine. The former plus a 48-letter witness does not imply that 47 or fewer letters are impossible or that only two shortest strings occur. Extension-extremality concerns insertions, not block-factorization minimizers.

value.rationale: The first realizable length and exact minimizer/factorization count are intrinsic extremal invariants of the same natural binary nine-square class singled out by the sharp 2026 ten-square obstruction. Complete lower-bound enumeration and rigidity turn a known existence example into a unique extremal classification up to binary symmetries, rather than an arbitrary sampled cutoff. The result is exact and potentially useful as a benchmark for square-factorization automata and overlap-free language enumeration. No general structural theorem about longer products is claimed.
